change: Weight as power family plays^alpha; added raw-capped and hit-indicator return metrics; continuous-parameter sweep policy
why: Robert asked about log/exponent transforms and continuous vs discrete parameters

change: Benchmark peers = other users' bets in the same month x popularity bin (all computed leave-one-out), rather than "random artists of that popularity"
why: Clarification while implementing: makes leave-one-out symmetric for the bet and its peers; excess return = how your bets did vs everyone else's comparable bets

change: Weeks map to months by their midpoint; market observed only to 2012-12
why: Implementation detail; data thin out in 2013

change: Durability (C): artists not found on ListenBrainz count as 0 listeners (main); dropping them is a variant
why: 12% of artists missing, almost all tiny (30% of 1-4-listener artists, 0.4% of 5000+), so missing ~ never listened

change: Scenes: co-listening clusters partly encode *when* artists got popular (scene explains 10-29% of variance in artists' peak year; e.g. Skrillex, Gotye, Foster the People grouped — all 2011 breakouts). Proposed: genre-based scenes (MusicBrainz genres; 86% of plays covered, but only 9-18% of small artists) with untagged artists assigned by their listeners' earlier listening; current clusters kept as a contrast
why: Within-scene benchmarks would otherwise compare breakouts to breakouts and hide foresight

change: Scenes: year-by-year co-listening, 200 scenes (main) (each year's relatedness uses only earlier listening; artists existing before the year keep their pre-period co-listening position, new/small artists are placed by their listeners' earlier taste). Variants: 50 / 1000 scenes; all-years co-listening and genre-tag scenes as contrasts. Replaces the genre-tag proposal above
why: Robert preferred relatedness (co-listening) over labels; the actual problem was using future listening. Chosen on taste-independent quality criteria (analysis/out/scene_quality.txt): relatedness lift 9.0x vs 8.5x for the leaky all-years version (which was even fitted in-sample), with ~half the timing leak (0.11 vs 0.20); genre tags cover only 57% of bets. A first version had one catch-all scene holding 20-63% of listening (popular artists' diverse audiences average to a generic point) — fixed before comparison. Bets in 2005 have no scene (no earlier data)

change: Added momentum control: benchmark cells also by quintile of the artist's prior 6-month fixed-panel growth (leave-one-out). Artist-age cells (months since first listened; pre-2005 artists censored as one group) implemented as already specified
why: Standard factor control from finance (Carhart momentum) that should have been in the spec: adopting artists that are already rising earns returns without foresight. Together with scene and age controls, tests whether the primary signal is "style exposure" rather than skill
prompted_by_results: yes — the primary run showed a strong signal (skill share 0.62, cross-period persistence 0.25), which prompted a search for mechanical explanations

change: Controls (scene, age, momentum) applied additively (main): month x popularity-bin cells, then leave-one-out month x scene / month x age / month x momentum adjustments, backfitted. Fully crossed cells kept as a contrast only
why: Crossing all controls made cells tiny (8 artists per cell; 26% of bets in cells with a single artist), so bets were compared mostly to other people adopting the *same* artist, which mechanically erases artist-choice signal (persistence 0.13 crossed vs 0.23 additive). Each run now reports cell diagnostics
prompted_by_results: yes — the unexpectedly large drop with all controls crossed prompted the diagnosis

change: Model B uses taste communities instead of each user's k nearest neighbours: a user's community in year Y = users sharing their home scene, the scene they are most over-represented in during the previous 12 months (share of their plays / everyone's share, among scenes with >= 5% of their plays). Outcome = ln((later community adopters + 0.5) / community members active throughout); always adjusted additively for the artist's prior popularity within the community (deciles)
why: k-NN over 297k users x 36M bets (~7B lookups) was impractical. A first version used plain argmax of plays and put most users into a few big mainstream scenes (bet-weighted mean community ~26k users vs ~1.5k intended), so communities reflected popularity rather than taste; fixed before any B results

change: Variants with ~2-8x more bets (no onboarding cutoff, 2-week commitment, every first listen) run on a random half of users (hash), compared against the main controlled version on the same half
why: They exceed the machine's memory/disk budget at full size; half the users (~120k scored) is ample for persistence estimates

change: Sweep results so far (explore): persistence across separate periods stays 0.14-0.19 across onboarding, commitment window, horizon, weights, smoothing, bins and scene definitions; dating at first listen inflates it to 0.23 (trend-following credited as foresight, as predicted); a yes/no "hit" metric shows ~0.01
Model B also adjusted (additively) for month x community: the community's overall adoption rate that month
why: First B run showed very high persistence (0.33 across separate periods) that the impostors explained more of after controls (R^2 0.08 -> 0.21) — consistent with B rewarding membership in communities that adopt a lot, a stable trait of where you sit rather than foresight. B's outcome counts later adopters in *your* community, so the community's own rate must be the benchmark. Earlier B results kept as model_B/*_v1_no_community_fx
